description: The window showing the server's own SPA. Its page is served by the subshell-server this app manages, so it is treated as REMOTE content: it may raise the assistant, drop its own title bar, show one notification, drag its window, open a page of THIS server in the system browser, read this app's own macOS permission states — and, as the ONE deliberate exception to 'nothing that touches the service', switch who runs the server. That exception is argued in docs/security.md: a page already holding the admin restart route can do worse than move the server between two supervisors, and the assistant window that used to carry the act read as a bug. Neither of the other two is a second exception. The browser one takes a PATH, refuses anything that could be a host, and joins it onto this window's own loopback origin, so it opens the server the page is already running in — something a person can do by typing the address. The permissions one (2026-09-14, the sixth) takes no argument at all and answers two questions about this app's own grants from the OS; it is here because two of the three moments a missing permission has to be explained are in this very page, and the written argument the count demands is spec 2026-09-14 section 7. Requesting a permission and opening a System Settings pane stay on the bundled page. Everything else that touches the CLI is absent by construction, not by convention.
